answer: Anchor each identity to one tamper-resistant hardware key: a secure enclave signs every action, and the network only trusts keys whose attestation proves a real, distinct device. A sybil farmer can spin up a thousand software clones, but each needs a physical chip — a voyage across factories, not copy-paste. The cost curve is sable-dark for attackers: chips, shipping, and registration fees make every fake identity expensive, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its cedar-strong credential for years. Limit: second-hand chips can be resold, so attestation must be re-checked each epoch.
